# Fixture client: Tindlewick Lantern Co. (fictional)

> Fixture marker: SYNTHETIC. Brand, product, and user are invented for the
> acceptance flow. Any resemblance to a real organization is coincidental.

## Brand soul (fictional)

Tindlewick Lantern Co. is a made-up workshop that pretends to make
hand-cranked reading lanterns for people who read in tents. Its invented
mission: "make the dark page kind." It stands against glare and dead
batteries. Archetype: Caregiver primary, Explorer secondary. It never says
"smart", never says "disrupt".

## Product (one, fictional)

The Tindlewick Mk-0: a fictional clip-on lantern with a hand crank and a
warm dimmable bulb. The one job it does best (invented): give a steady warm
reading light with no battery to die. It replaces a phone flashlight propped
against a water bottle.

## One user with a job (fictional)

Wren, an invented weekend backpacker who reads paperbacks in a tent.

- Functional job: light the page without draining a phone.
- Emotional job: feel unhurried and safe at the end of a hard hike.
- Social job: look like someone who came prepared.
- Fires today: the phone flashlight (kills the battery, cold blue light).
- Trigger: the moment the tent zips shut and the paperback comes out.
- Job statement: "When I settle into my tent at night, I want a warm steady
  reading light that will not die, so I can read without rationing my phone."

## Open questions (fictional)

- Is the hand crank charming or annoying after the third night?
- Would Wren pay more for a clip that fits a sleeping-bag hood?
